page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the ecs.t5 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. The hardware configuration features 2 burstable vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core operating at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that this instance operates in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yields a score of 1057.79, categorized as weak, while the multi-core CPU performance drops to a poor rating at 2090.03. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached read bandwidth at 16.3 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.44 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect these limitations, registering 870.0 for single-core and 1493.0 for multi-core workloads. These metrics highlight the performance tradeoffs inherent in shared, burstable CPU allocations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.t5-c1m4.large offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require continuous CPU utilization. The burstable CPU model allows users to pay a lower baseline rate while retaining the ability to handle occasional spikes in demand. Given the poor to weak benchmark results across computational, memory, and database tests, this instance is suited for low-traffic web serving, basic code repositories, lightweight background tasks, or development and testing environments rather than resource-intensive production applications.
